name: The Gold, the Glory and the Statuette: World Prizes
description: From Olympic laurel to Nobel medals and Oscar statuettes: how rewards for courage, talent and genius became part of the story of our age.

checkpoints.name: Laurel and honour
checkpoints.note: The Ancient Olympic Games crowned winners with olive leaves. Later rulers rewarded loyalty and valour with the Order of the Garter, the Legion of Honour and the Iron Cross.

checkpoints.name: Medals for valour
checkpoints.note: The Medal of Honor and the Victoria Cross reward courage in war. The first modern Olympics of 1896 would go on to give medals for sport.

checkpoints.name: The Nobel century
checkpoints.note: Alfred Nobel's will creates the Nobel Prize and Nobel Peace Prize. Winners include Marie Curie, Rabindranath Tagore and Albert Einstein, while the Pulitzer Prize and Fields Medal honour writers and mathematicians and Jesse Owens wins four golds in Berlin.

checkpoints.name: Lights, camera, trophy
checkpoints.note: Hollywood's Academy Awards, the first held in 1929, spread to the Golden Globes, Emmys and Grammys. The Ballon d'Or honours Pelé, the Booker Prize and Palme d'Or honour books and films, and Martin Luther King Jr. wins the Peace Prize in 1964. The Pritzker Prize begins honouring architects in 1979.

checkpoints.name: New names on the list
checkpoints.note: Nelson Mandela and Malala Yousafzai win the Peace Prize, Zaha Hadid becomes a Pritzker winner, and Nadia Comăneci, Michael Phelps and Usain Bolt are Olympic stars. The Turing Award, the Abel Prize and a Fields Medal for Maryam Mirzakhani show how prizes now reach new fields.
